brief.headline: Memory stocks in bear territory; HBM3E dominates 2026 despite pricing fatigue and Samsung beat fails to impress
brief.summary: <cite index="40-7,40-11">Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix entered bear markets (>20% off highs), with semiconductors losing ~$1.5 trillion in market value since June 25</cite>. <cite index="39-1,44-1">Samsung's Q2 operating profit of ~$58B (19x YoY, +1,800% guidance) triggered 7-10% selloffs as investors question AI spend sustainability</cite>. <cite index="12-1">Q3 2026 DRAM contract prices projected +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15%, decelerating from Q1's record 90-95% surge</cite>. <cite index="7-18,7-24">HBM3E remains flagship in 2026; SK Hynix expected to capture ~70% HBM4 share on Nvidia Rubin, while Samsung closed HBM4 qualification gap</cite>. <cite index="28-5,28-7">CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026, with TSMC capacity reaching 120-140k wafers/month</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Fade near-term alpha in SK Hynix vs Samsung; risk/reward compressing. SK Hynix's 57% Q4 2025 HBM revenue share and 70% projected HBM4 allocation on Rubin is well-owned after 1,000%+ 12-month run. Samsung closed HBM4 qualification with 'Samsung is back' commentary from Nvidia customers, but Q3 2025 share was 35% vs 53% for Hynix—gap is structural but narrowing faster than consensus. Both names sold off 7-14% on Samsung's monster beat (implying bars are too high), and profit-taking dominates despite capacity additions (M17 from Hynix, P5 from Samsung, both 2027-2028). Relative call: neutral to slight Samsung outperform on mean reversion + lower valuation after drawdown, but conviction low; sector beta overwhelms stock-specific alpha in current tape. Watch HBM ASP trajectory and hyperscaler allocation shifts Q3.

memory_cycle.notes: Contract pricing still rising but decelerating sharply (Q3 DRAM +13-18% vs Q1 +90-95%). Demand bifurcation: AI/server tight, consumer destruction real (smartphone units -14% 2026E). HBM consuming 3x DDR5 wafer capacity per bit, structurally tightening commodity DRAM. Suppliers prioritizing margin over volume; no panic capacity adds until 2027-28 fabs online. Consensus peak ASP call now mid-2026 vs prior 2027 estimates. Hyperscaler LTAs capping server DRAM upside. Spot market activity cooling despite green headline prints—behavioral inflection precedes price inflection. Memory shortage real; market patience exhausted.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="7-15,7-16">BofA estimates 2026 HBM market at $54.6B (+58% YoY); Goldman sees ASIC-based HBM demand surging 82%, reaching 1/3 of market</cite>. <cite index="4-1,4-4">HBM3E accounts for ~2/3 of 2026 shipments as HBM4 ramps; adopted by Nvidia Blackwell Ultra, Google TPU v7p/v7e, AWS ASICs</cite>. <cite index="3-3">Q4 2025 revenue share: SK Hynix 57%, Samsung 22%, Micron 21%</cite>. <cite index="4-11,4-12">SK Hynix M15X fab (Cheongju) pilot ops May 2026, producing HBM3E and HBM4 with 1c DRAM for HBM4E</cite>. <cite index="10-2,10-3">Intel/SoftBank ZAM (Zero-Angle Memory) emerging as potential HBM-killer with 2-3x HBM3 bandwidth at lower cost/power; commercialization timeline unclear</cite>. Supply remains tightest chokepoint in AI infrastructure despite CoWoS easing.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix plunge 7-14% despite Samsung record profit; memory stocks enter bear market
news_pulse.implication: Profit-taking overwhelms fundamentals. Samsung Q2 op profit $58B (19x YoY) failed to satisfy after 145% YTD run. Semis down $1.5T since June 25. Validates 'good news priced in' thesis; bars unsustainably high.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix CEO announces ₩100T ($64B) investment: M17 NAND fab + P&T7 packaging plant, ops by 2029
news_pulse.implication: ₩80T for M17 (NAND), ₩20T for P&T7 (advanced packaging). Reinforces '2027-2028 no relief' timeline for capacity. Positive LT but pressures ST margins via capex intensity.

news_pulse.headline: South Korea unveils ₩800T ($518B) semiconductor ecosystem; Samsung, Hynix each building 2 new fabs
news_pulse.implication: National strategic push. Samsung 10-year ₩1,000T plan includes ₩300T new fabs + ₩350T AI datacenters. Shares fell on announcement—market fears capex cycle, not celebrating capacity.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex $600-700B, up 36% YoY; ~75% ($450B) AI infrastructure
news_pulse.implication: Amazon $200B, Microsoft $120B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $125-145B, Oracle $50B. Demand signal intact but investor skepticism rising on ROI. Memory beneficiary but capex-to-revenue gap widening triggers repricing.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM Q3 contract prices +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15%: deceleration from Q1 record +90-95%
news_pulse.implication: Pricing power intact but moderating. Consumer demand destruction (-14% smartphone shipments 2026E) vs enterprise strength. Spot activity cooling despite rising contract prices—behavioral red flag.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply gap narrows to 10% by end-2026 from 20%; capacity 120-140k wafers/month
news_pulse.implication: Easing bottleneck positive for HBM volume ramp. Nvidia locked 60% 2026 capacity (~800-850k wafers). Relief arrives 2027+ as CAGR >80% 2022-27. Shifts constraint from packaging back to memory die supply.

news_pulse.headline: Intel/SoftBank ZAM memory 2-3x HBM3 bandwidth, lower cost/power; VLSI paper June
news_pulse.implication: Existential risk to HBM roadmap if commercialized at scale. SAIMEMORY presenting at IEEE June 14-18 Honolulu. Timeline unclear but could disrupt 2027+ pricing assumptions if proven.

news_pulse.headline: BofA: 2026 memory supercycle similar to 1990s; DRAM revenue +51% YoY, NAND +45%, ASPs +33%/26%
news_pulse.implication: BofA names SK Hynix 'Top Pick'. 2026 memory market $551B, 2027E $843B. Supercycle thesis underpins valuations but current selloff suggests investors front-ran thesis; now pricing risk of 2027 correction.

brief.derivatives_signal: Implied volatility elevated post-selloff but no clear directional edge. KOSPI 200 futures risk-off; USD/KRW stability suggests local factor vs macro. ADR discounts widening (SSNLF/HXSCL) reflect overnight KRX weakness. Options flow would show whether this is profit-taking or structural repositioning—absent that data, assume tactical de-risking into SK Hynix US listing Friday. No conviction for immediate bounce; wait for hyperscaler Q2 earnings (late July) and DRAM spot stabilization.
watch_for_next_3h: SK Hynix US ADR listing Friday (7/11)—tests whether appetite for memory exposure persists or marks cycle top
Any hyperscaler capex guidance revisions or AI spending commentary (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon earnings late July)
DRAM spot price action (DDR4/DDR5) and NAND eMMC/UFS quotes—contract lags spot, so directional signal lives in spot market
Samsung/Hynix mgmt commentary on HBM4 customer mix and ASP trajectory vs HBM3E—critical for 2H26 margin assumptions
Chinese memory (CXMT, YMTC) capacity/share data—risk of oversupply post-2027 if China ramps aggressively
